subject: microbiology
title: Toxoplasma gondii, Ring Lesions and Intraerythrocytic Babesia

steps.tx: The coccidian apicomplexan **Toxoplasma gondii** infects virtually all warm-blooded vertebrates, but domestic cats and other felids serve as the sole definitive hosts where sexual coccidian schizogony occurs. Infected felines excrete millions of unsporulated oocysts into the environment in cat feces. Following environmental sporulation over one to five days, infective oocysts persist in moist soil and water for over a year.
steps.say: Felines are the sole definitive hosts, shedding environmentally hardy oocysts in cat feces.

vis.caption: Toxoplasma gondii crescentic tachyzoite morphology compared with blood protozoa [Credit: CDC, StewardMD cleared]

steps.tx: Humans acquire infection by ingesting undercooked meat containing resting **tissue cysts** (bradyzoites) from livestock, or by accidentally ingesting feline fecal oocysts from unwashed vegetables, contaminated soil, or domestic cat litter boxes. In the human small intestine, excystation releases rapidly dividing crescent-shaped tachyzoites that actively invade nucleated host cells, establishing acute haematogenous dissemination throughout deep visceral organs.
steps.say: Undercooked meat containing tissue cysts or cat oocysts transmit Toxoplasma to humans.

left.title: Tachyzoites (acute stage)
points: Rapid binary fission inside nucleated cells
Destroys host cells, driving acute tissue damage

right.title: Bradyzoites (chronic stage)
points: Slow-growing dormant stage within tissue cysts
Enclosed by tough spherical cyst membrane
Persists lifelong in brain, retina, and skeletal muscle

steps.tx: In patients with advanced human immunodeficiency virus and helper T-cell counts falling below one hundred cells per microlitre, dormant cerebral bradyzoites reactivate, causing necrotizing toxoplasmic encephalitis. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging demonstrates multiple, spherical **ring-enhancing lesions** with extensive surrounding vasogenic oedema, preferentially clustered within the basal ganglia, thalamus, and hemispheric corticomedullary junctions.
steps.say: Multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions targeting the basal ganglia signify reactivated toxoplasmic encephalitis in AIDS.

rows: Thin, smooth, uniform peripheral ring enhancement
Thick, irregular, nodular or patchy enhancement
Strongly positive for EBV DNA via PCR assay

steps.tx: Several round lesions that brighten as rings in the basal ganglia, with wide surrounding oedema, fit reactivated cerebral toxoplasmosis. In advanced HIV, once helper T cells fall below 100 per microlitre, dormant bradyzoites resume growth and cause necrotizing encephalitis. Contrast imaging shows multiple spherical **ring enhancing lesions** and vasogenic oedema. They prefer the basal ganglia, the thalamus, and the junctions between cortex and white matter. A solitary tumour does not follow that clustered pattern.
steps.say: When CD4 counts fall below 100, toxoplasma cysts in the brain reactivate. Scans then show several ring enhancing lesions with swelling around them, especially in the basal ganglia, thalamus, and at the edge of the cortex.

vis.alt: Contrast brain magnetic resonance imaging shows several ring enhancing lesions in the basal ganglia with surrounding oedema.
vis.caption: Multiple spherical lesions enhance as rings in the basal ganglia, and vasogenic oedema surrounds them. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Primary maternal infection acquired during pregnancy leads to transplacental vertical transmission, producing congenital toxoplasmosis. The classical **Sabin triad** comprises chorioretinitis, obstructive hydrocephalus, and diffuse intracranial periventricular calcifications. Chorioretinitis produces pigmented macular scars with vitritis, often described as a headlight in the fog on fundoscopic examination.
steps.say: The Sabin triad consists of chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, and intracranial periventricular calcifications.

rows: Focal necrotizing retinitis with pigmented scar
Severe visual loss; recurrent retinal reactivation
Diffuse scattered nodular and periventricular calcifications
Petechial rash mimicking blueberry muffin syndrome

steps.tx: The definitive first-line therapeutic regimen for cerebral toxoplasmosis is oral **pyrimethamine** combined with sulfadiazine, co-administered with oral folinic acid (leucovorin) to prevent bone marrow myelosuppression from dihydrofolate reductase inhibition. Clinical and radiological improvement should be evident within ten to fourteen days; failure to respond mandates brain biopsy to exclude primary central nervous system lymphoma.
steps.say: Pyrimethamine and sulfadiazine combined with folinic acid provide definitive first-line medical therapy.

nodes.label: Presumptive toxoplasmic encephalitis: multiple ring-enhancing lesions on MRI
Initiate pyrimethamine plus sulfadiazine plus oral folinic acid
Repeat neuroimaging at 14 days: lesion regression confirms diagnosis

steps.tx: The zoonotic tick-borne intraerythrocytic protozoan **Babesia microti** is transmitted by the bite of the Ixodes scapularis blacklegged tick in the northeastern United States, sharing the same vector as Lyme disease. Trophozoites invade host erythrocytes directly without undergoing any hepatic exo-erythrocytic schizogony, causing acute haemolytic anaemia, high fever, drenching sweats, and hemoglobinuria.
steps.say: Ixodes tick bites transmit Babesia microti directly into red blood cells, triggering acute haemolysis.

left.title: Babesia microti
points: Transmitted by Ixodes scapularis deer tick
No hepatic exo-erythrocytic stage; direct red cell entry
Severe, life-threatening haemolysis in asplenic patients

steps.tx: On Giemsa-stained thin blood films, Babesia trophozoites appear as delicate, pleomorphic intra-erythrocytic rings that closely resemble Plasmodium falciparum ring forms. However, Babesia is definitively distinguished by the complete absence of intracellular hemozoin pigment, the absence of gametocytes, and the pathognomonic formation of four daughter merozoites joined together in a cross-shaped **Maltese cross** tetrad.
steps.say: A cross-shaped tetrad of four merozoites resembling a Maltese cross definitively identifies Babesia.

rows: Completely absent; schizonts form rounded morula
Absent entirely; no dark crystal biocrystallization
Prominent golden-brown to black hemozoin pigment
Absent in circulating human blood films
Pyriform merozoites visible free in plasma
Extracellular merozoites rarely seen on smear

steps.tx: Asplenic patients, elderly individuals, and immunocompromised hosts suffer catastrophic, life-threatening babesiosis characterized by profound intravascular haemolysis, acute renal failure, and non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema. First-line therapy for mild to moderate babesiosis is oral **atovaquone plus azithromycin** for seven to ten days, whereas severe fulminant haemolytic infection requires intravenous clindamycin combined with oral quinine alongside urgent automated red cell exchange transfusion.
steps.say: Atovaquone plus azithromycin is first line, while severe disease in asplenic hosts warrants exchange transfusion.

nodes.label: Confirm intraerythrocytic Maltese cross tetrads on thin blood film
Mild to moderate disease: oral atovaquone plus oral azithromycin for 7-10 days
Severe infection with parasitaemia >10%: IV clindamycin + quinine + exchange transfusion
